text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose slightly today (up 0.28%), but the real story is the 9.87% jump over the past two weeks — driven by a sharp spike in crude oil prices. Brent crude topped $109 per barrel on October 19th after Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed attacks on Saudi Arabian airports and oil facilities, with further escalation in the Strait of Hormuz adding to supply concerns. U.S. crude is now trading at $101.91 per barrel, and refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, meaning higher crude prices translate directly into stronger profit margins for refiners like Marathon.

The recent uptick reflects how refiner stocks respond to oil price volatility tied to geopolitical risk. While oil prices have wobbled — falling slightly on October 20th on hopes for Middle East diplomacy — the underlying supply concerns from Houthi attacks remain unresolved, keeping crude elevated and supporting refiner economics. With U.S. storage levels sitting at normal-to-tight levels (698.56 million barrels of crude, 208 million of gasoline), tight market conditions continue to favor margins.
